name: tracker-recurring-recovery
goal: Recover recurring wakes and job receipts across an interrupted tick while keeping the occurrence history readable by the pinned legacy runner.

evidence: A failed enqueue must retain the stable wake identity after an atomic catch-up. After a lost job reply, a reopened worker must adopt the original receipt and update history and last result once.
The baseline parsed cron but did not exercise occurrence recovery or job adoption. The initial recurring service method cases use SQLite, a fixed clock and injected job and queue ports.
Test-only replay at 39455d3bc3 uses the identical tree as historical 47c58605c4. Both cases failed: the recurring tick and box_jobs schema were absent. Checkpoint c587357de5e6.
Advance occurrence history, due and durable intent in one SQLite transaction. Recover stable wake requests and claimed job receipts after interruption.
The same two method cases passed at 7f1476c995, byte-identical to the historical fix tree at 0dd6bd9393. Checkpoint 3fb15d1fada7.
